## TL;DR

Fixed dependency handling for task IDs at and above 1000. The frontmatter writer now quotes numeric-looking strings, while the dependency parser also accepts legacy bare YAML numbers and normalizes numeric IDs to the repository's minimum four-digit width. Regression coverage checks writing and parsing IDs `0658`, `1047`, and `12345`, including a legacy `depends_on: [1047]` entry becoming a blocker. The scoped RepoOS check passed.

## Work and rationale

The failure crossed two layers. `serializeTask` wrote a dependency ID such as `1047` as an unquoted YAML number because the common scalar serializer only quoted strings when YAML syntax required it. Later, dependency parsing intentionally accepted string entries only, so that serialized number disappeared from the parsed task. CLI validation could not catch the issue because it ran before serialization and therefore saw the original string input.

I fixed the general serialization behavior in `src/core/frontmatter.ts`. Numeric-looking strings are now emitted with quotes, preserving their string type when YAML is read back. This applies consistently to string scalars passed through the shared writer rather than special-casing only `depends_on`; it prevents the same type loss for other string fields using that serializer. Existing quoting behavior remains in place for values that need quoting for other YAML reasons.

The parser change in `src/core/task-dependencies.ts` makes old files work without rewriting them. It accepts numeric dependency list entries and numeric `id` fields in mapping entries, converts them to strings, and pads digit-only numeric values to at least four characters. Padding is deliberately limited to values parsed as YAML numbers. Quoted string IDs retain their exact spelling: an existing string such as `"0"` must not become `"0000"`, and IDs longer than four characters such as `12345` remain unchanged.

Tests cover writer/parser round trips for `0658`, `1047`, and `12345`; legacy numeric values including `1047` and `658`; mapping-form numeric IDs; and a task with a bare numeric dependency being reported as blocked. The blocked-state test exercises the same dependency calculation used by list and task payload reporting, while the existing dependency-gate route tests cover the Start conflict response described in `docs/task-dependencies.md`.

I documented the compatibility behavior in `docs/task-dependencies.md`: new writes preserve number-like IDs as quoted strings, old numeric entries are interpreted as strings with the repo's four-character minimum width, and no file migration is needed because the parser is tolerant.

I parsed the task files in this worktree's `work/` directory after the change. The scan covered the complete current corpus. The task specification references #1050 gaining `1047`, but the #1050 task file present in this worktree does not currently contain a `depends_on` entry. I left that file untouched as instructed. Thus the parser behavior is covered synthetically with the exact legacy syntax; there was no existing dependency entry in this corpus to observe changing from absent to `1047`.

## Approaches tried

The first implementation normalized every digit-only dependency value, including quoted strings. The required check caught a regression in an existing dependency test: the quoted ID `"0"` changed into `"0000"`. That demonstrated the distinction the parser must preserve between YAML numeric scalars and strings. I tightened normalization to apply only when the parsed value is a number, then reran the full required scoped check. The corrected behavior keeps explicitly quoted string IDs exact while repairing numeric scalars.

I also considered whether a one-time migration was needed for existing files. Since parsing can recover the numeric value without changing the source file, and the acceptance criteria require existing files to work without manual edits, a migration would add unnecessary churn. The documentation records why the parser's compatibility handling makes one unnecessary.

## Challenges and blockers

The primary challenge was preserving leading zeros and distinguishing a legacy numeric scalar from a quoted string. The writer fix prevents future loss of type; parser compatibility handles already-written files. The initial check failure exposed an overly broad normalization rule, which was corrected before the successful run.

The task specification names #1050 as a file expected to contain `depends_on: [1047]`, but the worktree copy inspected during this session has no dependency field. I did not synthesize or edit that task metadata. The equivalent raw numeric frontmatter is covered by regression tests, and the implementation will parse it when present. The requested hold release for #1050 remains a human/driver follow-up after this fix lands.

## Key learnings

YAML scalar spelling is part of the persistence contract when a field is semantically a string. Validation before writing is insufficient if serialization can silently change the value's type. Shared scalar writers should protect numeric-looking strings, and parsers for persisted task metadata should be tolerant of historical representations where practical.

Normalization should reflect information actually present in the parsed value. A numeric YAML scalar loses any original leading zeroes, so it can be padded to the repository's minimum ID width. A quoted string preserves its spelling and should remain unchanged. Keeping that distinction explicit avoids breaking valid short string IDs while repairing legacy numeric IDs.

The final command `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed remote validation. All scoped test suites passed (6,614 tests passed, one skipped), followed by the rendered contrast audit and UI smoke test. The gate also completed its build, formatting, and lint checks before the tests. No UI files changed. RepoOS will perform its server-side verification and finalize the handoff after this turn ends.
